title: I am a designer who cannot code. I shipped a calm block puzzle on iOS and Android with Claude. What the AI did, what it could not do, and the numbers so far
author: Gold-Adhesiveness574
selftext:
Commercial self promotion flair, so up front: this is my game, FALLMATCH, free, no ads, no IAP for now. Links at the bottom. The rest is the development story, because that is what this sub is for.

Background. I design for a living and have never written code. Earlier this year I started building a block puzzle with Claude and shipped it on both stores at the end of August. Every line of code was written by the model. My job was the design, the rules of the game, testing on real phones, and saying no a lot.

The thing I did not expect: the hard part was not getting code out of the AI, it was keeping the project coherent over months of sessions that forget each other. What worked was making the AI keep a ledger. Every session ends with it writing a handoff log, a feedback file and a daily plan into the project folder, and every session starts with it reading them. The rules we learned the hard way live there too. The build we tested is the build we ship, never a different one. Android gets tested first because every store build costs money. Permission and syntax checks run before every build. Without those files the second week would have undone the first.

The levels are the part that is not AI, and I think that is why the game holds up. The 3 star target on every board is the proven minimum number of moves, found by an exhaustive solver, not estimated by a model. Candidate boards go into a queue, a separate checker runs for hours on my home PC, two engines at a time because 16 GB of RAM is what I have, and only boards with a proof ship. 900 boards so far across a campaign and a ladder mode, plus one daily board that is the same for everyone.

Things that went wrong, in case it helps someone. The first audio library played sounds sometimes and not other times, so we replaced it with a Web Audio style engine that decodes each sound once and fires a fresh source every time. Small Android phones with large font settings broke the layout, and I only caught it because I test on a Samsung with display zoom and font size pushed to maximum. And every early player said the 3 star target was confusing, so a level start card now shows the target and which special moves that board needs before you play. That change came from player feedback on Reddit, not from me or the model.

Numbers, since people ask. Launched August 26, just over 100 downloads across both stores, all organic, zero revenue by design. The first paid test started yesterday, Apple Ads on a 100 dollar credit and a small Google App campaign. Total cash spent so far is under 200 dollars.

Happy to answer anything about the workflow, the solver, or what I would do differently.

App Store: [https://apps.apple.com/app/fallmatch/id6791134651](https://apps.apple.com/app/fallmatch/id6791134651)

Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.gusmediaworks.matcher](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.gusmediaworks.matcher)

comments.body:
Much better to write these posts yourself, imvho <3

The text is very Claude. I want to slap the presumptiousness out of it.

replies.author: Gold-Adhesiveness574
replies.body: Fair point. English is not my first language and I let Claude tidy the text, and it tidied me out of it too. The facts are mine, the tone is not. Which part felt presumptuous? I would rather fix it than argue.

replies.author: AlgaeNo3373
replies.body: Well if you are speaking a second language then actually, allow me to reverse course entirely and insist that you ignore my English-priviliged dumb ass! Claude has done a generally good job at translating. It's only a handful of things falling into "Claude-isms". Stuff like "since people have asked" etc. Maybe they actually have (asked, that is), but that asking could also be Claude just writing defensively, as Claude loves to do.

replies.author: Gold-Adhesiveness574
replies.body: Thanks, no offense taken. The asking part is real though, an editor emailed me this morning about money and downloads, and someone in the Dev Saturday thread asked how it will be monetized. So that one was me, not Claude being defensive.

replies.body:
